entities.label: TextOfTheConstitution
entities.rationale: The text of the Constitution is a specific information artifact — a pattern of meaningful linguistic content that can be copied, instantiated in multiple physical bearers (printed documents, digital files), and yet retains its identity as the same text across those copies. This is the hallmark of a generically dependent continuant (BFO_0000031). It is an individual (a particular text, not a kind of text), and it is most naturally classified under the existing working class 'Statute' (itself typed as BFO_0000031), since constitutions are foundational legal texts. The existing individual 'USConstitution' presumably refers to the document-as-institution or legal instrument; 'TextOfTheConstitution' refers specifically to the linguistic/textual content, so a new individual is warranted unless the user intends these to be identical.

relations.rationale: The text of the Constitution is an instance of Statute, a class of generically dependent continuants representing enacted legal texts.
The textual content is part of the broader constitutional instrument individual already in the ontology; the text is a constituent part of the Constitution as a generically dependent continuant.

open_questions: Should 'TextOfTheConstitution' be identified with the existing individual 'USConstitution', or is a distinct individual needed to separate the textual content from the constitutional instrument as a whole?
Is this the US Constitution specifically, or a generic/unnamed constitution? If the former, should the IRI be 'working:TextOfUSConstitution' for clarity?
Should we distinguish the 'text as enacted' (original 1787 text) from the 'text as amended' (current text including all amendments)? These could be separate individuals or a single evolving GDC.
proposal.rationale_summary: The text of the Constitution is classified as a generically dependent continuant (BFO_0000031) because it is an information artifact — a pattern of linguistic content whose identity is independent of any particular physical substrate and which can be multiply instantiated in different material bearers (paper copies, digital files, etc.). It is typed as an individual (a specific text) rather than a class, and falls under the existing working class 'Statute'. A 'part of' relation to the existing individual 'USConstitution' is proposed, modeling the text as a constituent part of the broader constitutional instrument already represented in the ontology, though the user should confirm whether these should remain distinct individuals or be merged.
